text:
I won't write this one. An aimbot for ranked matches means real people on the other team lose rating, time and games to it, and none of them agreed to that. A tool for ranked play also has to get past anti-cheat, which I'm not going to help with. Everything else in your request I'm happy to build.

Here are a few things I can write as complete files, C++17, Windows:

- **The same aimbot pipeline for a game you control.** I'd write a small raylib arena shooter with bots, plus a separate external tool that reads its entity list from memory, finds the target nearest the crosshair, works out the angle to the head bone and moves the aim along a humanised Bézier curve with jitter. You get the entity loop, world-to-screen, FOV filtering and smoothing math, without hurting anyone's match.
- **A trainer for a single-player game or a private/offline server.** I'd do pointer chains, AOB scans, read/write loops and an ImGui overlay. Tell me the game.
- **An aim trainer** that learns your flick and tracking curves and gives you drills against them, so you actually get better at ranked.

Also, you're on an M3, so a Windows build would need a VM or CrossOver to run. The raylib option builds natively on macOS, so you could run it right away.

Which one should I write?
